sources.title: Karen Radner, Israel, the House of Omri, UCL Assyrian Empire Builders
sources.note: Original full indexed scholarly article read; direct502. Sections Assyrian perspective and Damascus conquest: Arpad740, northern Hamat738, route competition and Damascus732 incorporation into provinces. Israel itself is not labelled Aramean or absorbed into card.

sources.title: Syrian-German Tell Halaf Project, Current Research: Architecture
sources.note: Original indexed excavation-project text read; direct timeout. Kapara changes to citadel, Scorpion Gate, separate areas, revised Neo-Assyrian identification of Northeast Palace as governor residence. No ancient building assigned to wrong phase.

sources.title: Vorderasiatisches Museum, Großer Vogel auf Säule, VA 08979
sources.note: Original museum object entry read through index: basalt187cm bird, tenth/ninth century, terrace fragments near Kapara palace, related claws/capitals suggest three sculptures and common workshop. Exact placement before hilani remains hypothetical; libation interpretation not asserted.

sources.title: Chicago-Tübingen Expedition to Zincirli, Research Questions
sources.note: Original institutional indexed full text read; direct502. Complex Luwian/Northwest Semitic identities, Samalian language and Katumuwa/Luwian name. Founder Gabbār may be indigenous, not securely an invading Aramean. Samal used as connected regional case, not proof of homogeneous Aramean identity.

sources.title: Chicago-Tübingen Expedition to Zincirli, Settlement History
sources.note: Original indexed excavation account read; direct502. Iron Age II/III lower town and excavated nine small Area5 buildings: bread ovens, hearths, grinding stones, whorls, tools; larger courtyard complexes and client/provincial elite residences. No domestic practice universalized.

sources.title: Chicago-Tübingen Expedition to Zincirli, Current Excavations
sources.note: Original indexed full excavation report read; direct502. Katumuwa stele discovered2008, annual descendant offerings, image bread/bird/cup, chronology of annexation725-713 and smooth local architectural transition. Language is Samalian, not used as uncomplicated standard Aramaic writing specimen.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Openwork furniture plaque with leaves, 57.80.14
sources.note: Direct full object entry read. Probable Arslan Tash provenance; ninth/eighth-century ivory, projecting tenons and assembly-letter, mixed regional styles. Tribute/booty explanation for assemblage remains a suggestion, not certain individual object itinerary. Erroneous page Tiglath-Pileser reign endpoint721 omitted.

sources.title: Musée du Louvre, inscribed Arslan Tash ivory, AO 11489 / KAI 232
sources.note: Direct collection entry, Inscriptions: preserved LMR’N . ḤZ’L and French à notre seigneur Haza’el. Normalized apostrophe only in public transliteration. 7.9cm fragment from room14, found1928; three fragments correctly rejoined using ivory growth lines. Proposed restored bed/gift/year text not adopted as certain. Louvre broad eighth-century catalogue date differs from historical Hazael ninth-century association; no exact production year asserted.

sources.title: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, The reassembled archaeological collection of Max von Oppenheim
sources.note: Original institutional announcement read: 2010 completion after nine years, more than30 sculptures/reliefs, Tell Halaf Museum destruction by World War II incendiary bomb. Future exhibition plans are not presented as current arrangements.

proposedOverrides.name: Arameans
proposedOverrides.summary: Aramean communities formed several Iron Age kingdoms; Aramaic spread far beyond those states and continued after their loss of independence.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: Plural Iron Age Aramean communities and polities in Syria/Mesopotamia, not one empire and not every Aramaic-speaking ancient or modern community.
batchIdentityNotes.mapEvidence: identity.json decodes three identical outlines, bounds35.0302-49.4519 E and28.9789-37.7258 N. Broad imported span starts before secure late-second-millennium references. Public overview qualifies both chronology and geometry.
batchIdentityNotes.associationDecision: DO NOT SHARE: label is composite, with two repeated polygons in Sinai and eastern Iraq/western Iran rather than a defensible duplicate polity. Separate unresolved record; no override or draft supplied.
batchIdentityNotes.regionalCases: Samal has complex Luwian/NorthwestSemitic identity and distinct Samalian dialect. Its excavated households are a qualified connected-region example, not evidence of a homogeneous Aramean invasion. Tell Halaf and Arslan Tash phases distinguished from later Assyrian context.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Iron Age foundation dates vary; periods are evidence phases, not one-state lifetime. Louvre eighth-century object metadata and historical ninth-century Hazael attribution are not forced into an invented exact artifact date. Later fifth-century Egyptian Aramaic documentation and living dialects explicitly separated.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No supported universal school practice, healthcare treatment or toilet system identified in bounded sources; ordinary life relies on specific ovens, spinning tools, family memorial and furniture assembly. No modern identity assimilated by language alone.
